preamble: Anaptyxis of [u] splits a consonant cluster with a rounded vowel that matches the u before it. Turkish does this to Arabic loans ending in a consonant cluster after u: Arabic nuṭq 'speech' and ʕuḍw became nutuk 'speech, oration' and uzuv 'organ'. The vowel is absent before a vowel-initial suffix (definite accusative nutku, uzvu), and Ottoman Turkish kutb 'pole', colloquially kutub, gave kutup in the same way.

examples.note: Borrowed through Ottoman Turkish نطق, listed as nutuk or nutk; before a vowel-initial suffix the stem is nutk- (definite accusative nutku).
Borrowed through Ottoman Turkish عضو (uzv); definite accusative uzvu. Ottoman Turkish قطب kutb 'pole' (colloquial kutub) gave kutup /kuˈtup/ with the same vowel.
